TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 28.10.2019 PASSED BY THE MOTOR ACCIDENTS CLAIMS TRIBUNAL-II,
BALLARI IN M.V.C.NO.631/2018 WITH COST IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

IN THESE APPEALS ARGUMENTS BEING HEARD ON 27.09.2023 AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT, THIS DAY,
COMING ON FOR "PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT", THIS DAY,
BASAVARAJA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

Both appeals arise out of the judgment and award dated 28.10.2019 passed in MVC.No.631/2018 by the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal-II, Ballari (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2.
Parties herein are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Brief facts of the claim petition are that, on 26.12.2017 at about 10.30 p.m., Vinay Kumar was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing No.KA-35/J-2551 from Bhujanga Nagar towards Donimalai,
Sandur Taluk, at that time respondent No.1,being the driver of the Heavy Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA- 35/B-5715, came from opposite direction in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of Vinay Kumar, as a result, he fell on the road, sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.

Thereafter, postmortem was conducted at Taluka Public Hospital, Sandur, then the petitioners took the body of the deceased and performed funeral and other rituals at their native place and have spent Rs.50,000/-.

Further, it is contended that prior to the accident deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 25 years, was diploma graduate as well as an agriculturist and earning Rs.3,00,000/- per annum and maintaining his family.

Due to untimely death of Vinay Kumar,
petitioners have lost earning member in the family, dependency, love and affection, loss of estate,
loss of social security and suffering mentally, physically and financially.
It is further contended that the accident in question was entirely due to rash and negligent driving of the Lorry by its driver.
Respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.3 being the insurer of said vehicle are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
On all these grounds sought for allowing of the claim petition.
4. In pursuance of service of notice, respondents Nos.1 to 3 have appeared through their respective counsel.
Respondent No.1 has not filed any objection.
Respondent No.2 has filed his objection contending that respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner of offending lorry, lorry is insured with respondent No.3.
Respondent No.3 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Further, he has denied all the averments made in the claim petition and sought for dismissal of the petition.
5.
Respondent No.1 has adopted the objections filed by respondent No.2.

6. The respondent No.3-Insurance Company has filed separate statement of objection contending that offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3, but respondent No.2 has not informed about the accident in question.

It is further contended that as on the date of accident, respondent Smt.Shailaja W/O Late. Vinay Kumar vs T.Alibaba S/O T., Basha Sab on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28076762/
4 No.1 was not holding effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle.

In FIR, nowhere it is mentioned about the vehicle number and name of the driver, the vehicle of the respondent No.2 has not involved in the accident, the petitioners with malafide intention, implicated the said vehicle in this case.
The accident in question occurred due to negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased.
Further, they have denied all the averments made in the claim petition and sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of rival pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether petitioners prove that on alleged date, time, place the respondent No.1 drove the offended Heavy Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No. KA35/B-5715 in high speed,
rash and negligent manner and caused accident, due to it, deceased- Vinay Kumar sustained injuries and later on succumbed to the said injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what extent, from whom?
3. What order or award?
8. To substantiate the case of petitioners, petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.9.

On the other hand, authorized person of the respondent No.3 was examined as RW.1 and the Investigating Officer was examined as RW.2 and got marked Ex.D.1 and 2.
9.

On hearing the arguments, the Tribunal has given its findings to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1 :- Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3 :- As per final order 10.
In view of the findings given, the Tribunal has allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.15,82,000/- with interest at 7% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

Being aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has preferred appeal in MFA.No.
101171/2020 questioning the liability and claimants have preferred appeal in MFA.No.102165/2020 for enhancement of compensation.
SUBMISSION OF LEARNED COUNSEL FOR INSURANCE COMPANY 11.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of appellant- Insurance Company submits that the impugned Judgment and award is opposed to the law and facts on record and same is liable to be set aside.
The alleged accident has occurred on 26.12.2017 and the FIR was registered on 27.12.2017.

The FIR has been registered against an unknown vehicle by an unknown driver, however,
subsequently a lorry bearing No.KA-35/B-5715 has been falsely implicated in the accident to make the claim to appear as hit and run case.
That there is no eyewitness to the accident, and based only Smt.Shailaja W/O Late. Vinay Kumar vs T.Alibaba S/O T., Basha Sab on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28076762/
5 upon the statement of CW-4, the Police Officer and CW-5-owner of the vehicle, charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the said lorry.
The Tribunal is swayed away by the filing of the charge sheet and thereby erroneously saddled the liability against the appellant-insurer, which has resulted into miscarriage of justice.
As per the charge sheet, the accident is head-on collision between the motorcycle and the lorry.
If there is a head-on collision the damages would be to the front side of the both the vehicles, whereas the MVI report exhibit Ex.P-4 discloses that the rear bumper of the lorry has been bent.
That the Investigating Officer has examined as RW-2.
As per his statement, the occurrence of the accident by the lorry bearing No.KA-35/8-5715 has been informed by the owner of the Lorry on 11.01.2018.
The very statement of the said witness discloses that there is a collusion between the petitioners and owner of the vehicle in making the false claim.
Neither the death occurred due to self negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased nor was a hit and run.
On all these grounds, sought for allowing of its appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment and award.
SUBMISSION OF LEARNED COUNSEL FOR THE CLAIMANTS 12.

As against this, the learned counsel for the appellant- claimants submits that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts and fastened the liability upon Insurance Company.
There are no grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal as to the liability of Insurance Company.
Further, he submitted that the Tribunal has not awarded the just and proper compensation in accordance with law and facts and also decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.
On all these grounds sought for allowing of the appeal by enhancing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal and also prayed for dismissal of the appeal filed by the Insurance Company.

13. Having heard the arguments on both sides and on perusal of the records, the following points would arise for our consideration :
(1) Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the Insurance Company?
(2) Whether the appellant/claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
(3) What order or award?
14.

Our answer to the above points are as under :
Point No.1- in the negative.
Point No.2- Partly in affirmative.
Point No.3-as per the final order.
15. We have carefully examined the materials placed before this Court.
It is the case of the petitioners that on 26.12.2017 at about 10.30 p.m. Vinay Kumar was Smt.Shailaja W/O Late.

sentences.text: Postmortem was conducted at Taluka Public Hospital, Sandur and thereafter petitioners took the body.
Respondent No.2-owner of the vehicle has not disputed the accident.
He has clearly admitted that respondent No.1 was the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident, but has denied the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the lorry.
Therefore, it is clear that respondent Nos.1 and 2 have not disputed the accident in question.
But respondent No.3 has contended that the lorry bearing No.KA-35/B-5715 is not involved in the accident.
Petitioners have colluded with owner of the vehicle and also Police officials and filed false charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. To substantiate the case of the petitioners, Smt.Shailaja-petitioner No.1 examined as P.W.1, has clearly deposed as to the accident as alleged in the petition.
Apart from her oral evidence, she has produced the documents.

A perusal of the documentary evidence placed by the petitioners, it is clear that on the basis of complaint by one Sri Karibasappa, Sandur Police have registered the Crime no.254/2017 against unknown driver of the vehicle for the commission of offence under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of M.V.Act, 1988 and submitted the FIR to the Court.

Thereafter, Police visisted to the spot and conducted the spot panchanama and inquest panchanama of the deceased in the presence of panchas, obtained postmortem report, MVI report and recorded the statement of witnesses, recorded statement of complainant and other witnesses.

On thorough investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted the charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for the commission of offence under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

After filing of the charge sheet, learned Civil Judge and JMFC,
Sandur has taken cognizance against the driver of the offending vehicle for the commission of offence under Section 279, 304A of IPC and Section 187 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and a case came to be registered in Criminal Case No.353/2018.
17.

It is appropriate to mention here as to the claim notice issued by the Circle Inspector of Police,
Sanduru Circle, Ballari District under Rule 3(2) of the Motor Vehicle Accident Compensation Claims, which is marked as Ex.P.8.

In view of Rule 232(A) of Chapter VIII of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 the contents of the report submitted to the claims Tribunal in Form No.54 appended to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, Form No.63-B and confirmation under Clause B of Rule 232 by the Insurance Company shall be presumed to be correct and shall be read in evidence without formal proof, till proved to the contrary.

18. It is also relevant to mention here as to the provision of Rule 232 Chapter VII of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 which reads as under :
"232. Duties of Insurance Company.-It shall be the duty of the Divisional Manager or the Branch Manager of the Insurance Company, as expeditiously as possible, to- Smt.Shailaja W/O Late. (b) ascertain and verify facts about insurance of motor vehicle(s) involved in the accident and confirm the same to the Claims Tribunal within thirty days of receiving notice of the claim case:
(c) move application before the concerned registering authority in Form 63-A and gather information about the motor vehicle(s) involved, and the driving lience(s) held by the driver(s) thereof as per details mentioned in Form 63-B.

(d) deposit with the written statement in the Claims Tribunal, the amount equivalent to the compensation, awardable on the principle of no fault liability under Section 140 of the Act in such cases where the information received in Form 63 confirms death or permanent disability to have been caused as a result of the use of the motor vehicle covered by the insurance certificate/policy issued by its."
19.
In the case on hand, the Insurance Company has not placed any material before the Tribunal as to the compliance of Rule 232 of Chapter VII of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.

However, the Insurance Company has examined two witnesses before the Tribunal as RW.1 and 2.
RW.1 has not disputed the contents of Ex.P.8 the notice issued by the Circle Inspector of Police,
Sandurr Circle, as to the motor vehicle accident to the legal representatives of deceased.

RW.1-Balesh Ramagondi, Legal Executive, working in the respondent Insurance Company has deposed in his evidence that the petitioners have colluded with Police officials and they have managed to show the name of first respondent and the lorry bearing No.KA-34/B-5715 to the crime with a malafide intention to claim unjust compensation.
Further, he has deposed that the vehicle belonging to the first respondent has not at all caused the accident in question.
During course of cross-examination, he has clearly admitted that he has not questioned as to the charge sheet filed by the Investigating Officer.
He has also clearly admitted that respondent No.1 was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further, he has clearly admitted that they have appointed Investigating Officer to investigate the matter and he has also submitted report to the Insurance Company and same is not produced by them and he has not assigned any reason for non-production of investigation report before the Tribunal.
RW.1 has not whispered anything as to the compliance of mandatory provisions of Rule 232 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.

Apart from this, the Insurance Company has examined the Investigating Officer before the Tribunal as RW.2, who has clearly deposed as to the investigation conducted by him and also filing of the charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the commission of offence under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The Insurance Company has failed to rebut the statutory presumption as contemplated under Rule 232(A) of Chapter VII of the Karnataka Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.

Charge sheet submitted by the Investigating Officer has been proved along with the evidence of RW.2.

The Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts as to the liability of the Insurance Company.
On re-appreciation/re-examination of the evidence on record, we do not find any illegalities/infirmities in the findings given by the Tribunal as to the liability of the Insurance Company.
For the aforesaid reasons, we cannot accept the arguments advanced on behalf of the Insurance Company.
Accordingly, we answer point No.1 in negative.

21. Point No.2-With regard to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is concerned,
the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of deceased at Rs.7,500/- per month, which is not in consonance with the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
It is stated by the PW.1 that the deceased was aged about 25 years, he was diploma holder and was also an agriculturist and earning Rs.3,00,000/- per annum and maintaining family.

In this regard he has produced Ex.P.9-RTC extract pertaining to land bearing Sy.no.283 of Krishnanagar, Sanduru hobli,
which is standing in the name of one Smt Parvatamma W/o. G. Chandrappa.

Except this document,
petitioners have not produced any other document.
However, considering the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, it is just and proper to take the notional income of deceased at Rs.10,250/- per month.

It is not in dispute that deceased was aged 25 years as on the date of accident, hence 18 multiplier is applicable in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009)6 SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% of the income has to be added as future prospects, then it comes to Rs.10,250/- + 40% i.e., Rs.4,100/- = Rs.14,350/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Out of this 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.14,350/- - (1/3 i.e., Rs.4,783/-) = Rs.9,567/-.
Then, loss of dependency comes to Rs.9,567/- X 12 X 18 = Rs.20,66,472/-.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for enhancement of compensation towards loss of dependency.

22. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case and also keeping in mind the Judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pranay Sethi and Sarla Verma (supra), petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation as under :
1. Loss of dependency Rs.20,66,472/-
2. Loss of consortium.

Rs.1,20,000/-
(Rs.40,000/- X 3)
3. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
4. Towards funeral and Rs.15,000/-
transportation of dead body.

Total Rs.22,16,472/-

24. Point No.3- For the aforesaid reasons and discussions, we proceed to pass the following :
ORDER (i) Appeal of Insurance Company in MFA.No.101171/2020 is dismissed.
(ii) Appeal of claimants in MFA.No.102165/2020 is allowed in part modifying the judgment and award dated 28.10.2019 passed in MVC.No. 631/2018 by the Tribunal by enhancing the compensation to Rs.22,16,472/- from Rs.15,82,000/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum form the date of petition till its realization.
(iii) The respondent-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation with interest within a period of sixty days before the Tribunal from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
(iv) Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The alleged accident has occurred on 26.12.2017 and the FIR was registered on 27.12.2017.
The FIR has been registered against an unknown vehicle by an unknown driver, however,
subsequently a lorry bearing No.KA-35/B-5715 has been falsely implicated in the accident to make the claim to appear as hit and run case.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
A perusal of the documentary evidence placed by the petitioners, it is clear that on the basis of complaint by one Sri Karibasappa, Sandur Police have registered the Crime no.254/2017 against unknown driver of the vehicle for the commission of offence under Sections 279, 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of M.V.Act, 1988 and submitted the FIR to the Court.
Thereafter, Police visisted to the spot and conducted the spot panchanama and inquest panchanama of the deceased in the presence of panchas, obtained postmortem report, MVI report and recorded the statement of witnesses, recorded statement of complainant and other witnesses.
On thorough investigation, Investigating Officer has submitted the charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for the commission of offence under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
After filing of the charge sheet, learned Civil Judge and JMFC,
Sandur has taken cognizance against the driver of the offending vehicle for the commission of offence under Section 279, 304A of IPC and Section 187 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and a case came to be registered in Criminal Case No.353/2018.
17.
In the case on hand, the Insurance Company has not placed any material before the Tribunal as to the compliance of Rule 232 of Chapter VII of the Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.
RW.1 has not whispered anything as to the compliance of mandatory provisions of Rule 232 of the Karnataka Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.
Apart from this, the Insurance Company has examined the Investigating Officer before the Tribunal as RW.2, who has clearly deposed as to the investigation conducted by him and also filing of the charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the commission of offence under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The Insurance Company has failed to rebut the statutory presumption as contemplated under Rule 232(A) of Chapter VII of the Karnataka Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989.
Charge sheet submitted by the Investigating Officer has been proved along with the evidence of RW.2.

The Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts as to the liability of the Insurance Company.
On re-appreciation/re-examination of the evidence on record, we do not find any illegalities/infirmities in the findings given by the Tribunal as to the liability of the Insurance Company.
However, considering the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, it is just and proper to take the notional income of deceased at Rs.10,250/- per month.
It is not in dispute that deceased was aged 25 years as on the date of accident, hence 18 multiplier is applicable in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.) and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another, reported in (2009)6 SCC 121.
In view of Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% of the income has to be added as future prospects, then it comes to Rs.10,250/- + 40% i.e., Rs.4,100/- = Rs.14,350/-.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Out of this 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.14,350/- - (1/3 i.e., Rs.4,783/-) = Rs.9,567/-.
Then, loss of dependency comes to Rs.9,567/- X 12 X 18 = Rs.20,66,472/-.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for enhancement of compensation towards loss of dependency.
22. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case and also keeping in mind the Judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Pranay Sethi and Sarla Verma (supra), petitioners are entitled for enhanced compensation as under :
1. Loss of dependency Rs.20,66,472/-
2. Loss of consortium.

transportation of dead body.
Hence, we answer point No.2 partly in the affirmative.
